THE BULWARK: An American Life Cut Short
July 9, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Bill Kristol's center-right Bulwark on Lorenzo Salgado Araujo — 35 years in Houston, a business owner who put three sons through university, killed by ICE. Its verdict: he was "a better American" than the men who killed him. 🇲🇽

Worth marking when it happens: parts of the US press, left and right, are mourning the man Mexico is now filing charges over — not running the fear-copy the killing usually generates.

• "He deserved to live a quiet life… a husband, father and a job creator for dozens of men"
• "I dare say Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was a better American than they are"
• his sons' motto, from him: "Give it your all, and never give up"

NEWSCHANNEL 10: Sinaloa connection — 4 indicted in Amarillo-to-Mexico gun pipeline
July 9, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Four people in Amarillo, Texas indicted for running guns to the Sinaloa cartel — bought at a Cash America pawn shop on I-40 through straw purchases, then smuggled south. 🇲🇽

The same US press that brands the cartels "foreign terrorists" rarely dwells on where their rifles come from: American gun stores. Mexico has made this "iron river" argument for years.

• charged with "material support" to a "foreign terrorist organization"
• the guns "purchased by Hall" then "smuggled into Mexico"
• a straw purchase — a legal buyer fronting for someone who can't buy

HOUSTON CHRONICLE: Key witness in fatal ICE shooting faces deportation
July 13, 2026 | 🔴

📰 ICE shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo dead in a "mistaken identity" raid in Houston. Now his brother Victor — a key witness who says the agents never identified themselves — sits in detention, ordered removed to Mexico. 💀

Deport the witnesses and there's no one left to dispute ICE's account of how the homebuilder was killed driving his crew to a job site.

• "There are normal circumstances, and then there's what's going on here." — attorney Ruby Powers
• "I had to print off photos from the crime scene to show him in detention."
• "It's just shockingly, a totally different story." — Rep. Sylvia Garcia

📉🇲🇽 MEXICO'S INFLATION FALLS TO 3.37% — LOWEST IN FIVE AND A HALF YEARS

Annual inflation cooled to 3.37% in June, its lowest reading since December 2020 and inside Banxico's target range for a second straight month, INEGI reported. Fruit and vegetable prices fell 8.99% month-on-month, dragging monthly inflation to -0.27% — the first negative June in at least a decade, El Economista notes. Core inflation held at 4.03%. The "semáforo" of inflation turned green for the first time since 2020.

🌧️🇲🇽 RECORD RAINS HIT MEXICO CITY — 120 CREWS AND 49 MACHINES OUT WITHIN HOURS

Plan Tláloque 2.0 mobilized 120 personnel and 49 specialized machines — hydro-pneumatic trucks and suction units — as a record 12.5 million cubic meters of rain fell on Mexico City, 27.7 million across the metro zone. Iztapalapa's El Molino station clocked the heaviest at 31mm. Crews cleared 23% of flooding reports the same day, with Brugada ordering permanent monitoring across every city department while dam and river levels held stable.

🚨🇲🇽 FOUR CIA AGENTS DIED IN A CHIHUAHUA CAR CRASH — OPERATING WITHOUT MEXICAN AUTHORIZATION

An ordinary April 19 car accident in Chihuahua exposed four CIA agents working on Mexican soil with no federal authorization. Contralínea lays out the scale: between 800,000 and 1 million people work for US intelligence worldwide, backed by roughly 800 military bases — 80 to 100 of them in Latin America and the Caribbean. "The CIA is one of the principal espionage apparatuses the United States has, designed to maintain this imperialist power's presence for decades," said UNAM's Nayar López Castellanos.

⚽🇲🇽 MEXICO CITY HOSTED THE WORLD CUP — AND HAD ITS LEAST VIOLENT JUNE IN 15 YEARS

Clara Brugada calls the FIFA World Cup "the most demanding test for our security strategy in decades," and the capital passed it: daily homicides fell from 4.2 in June 2018 to 1.8 in June 2026 — a 57% drop, the safest June in fifteen years. Under her administration alone, homicides are down 31% in under two years. One in three killings simply stopped happening.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 TWO MEXICAN NAVY SHIPS DOCK IN VENEZUELA WITH 388 TONS OF AID

Two Mexican Navy vessels crossed eight days of Caribbean sea to reach La Guaira carrying 388 tons of humanitarian aid for Venezuelans hit by the June 24 earthquakes — food, bottled water, medicine, and four purification plants that each produce 1,000 liters of clean water an hour. A hundred Marine emergency responders are on the ground unloading and installing them. Ordered by President Sheinbaum as the quake toll reached 4,561 dead and nearly 18,000 homes destroyed.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO TAKES THE US TO ITS OWN COURTS OVER 17 DEAD IN ICE CUSTODY

Mexico formalized criminal complaints inside US district courts this Monday over the deaths of 17 Mexican nationals in ICE custody and operations — 14 died detained, three during raids. "We are moving from the diplomatic sphere directly to US district attorneys to demand the criminal investigation," said the SRE's Roberto Velasco. Six died of untreated medical conditions, including one man left a month in hyperglycemic crisis without ever being taken to a hospital.

🇲🇽🛢️ MEXICO ABSORBS THE OIL SPIKE SO DRIVERS DON'T

As global crude climbed, Hacienda raised the fuel subsidy for the week of July 11–17: the fiscal stimulus on Magna gasoline rose to 15.95% and on diesel to 26.26% — the highest of any fuel — with the state eating 1.06 and 1.93 pesos per liter through the IEPS "to keep fuel price increases from hitting consumers' wallets and feeding inflation." Premium, the luxury grade, gets no subsidy at all.
